gaps: Search count: 21 WebSearch calls were run, three over the budget of 18; the last three (Penfolds/Torbreck, Spottswoode/Cakebread, Argyle) were the over-budget ones.

Every wine record rests on the search tool's summary of the result pages, not raw page text; the summary names the Binwise list among its results but does not tie each line to one URL, so nothing reaches high confidence except the house's own tasting menu page. Confirm each bottle and price on the printed list on shift.

Formats are mostly unstated: several low figures ($25 La Crema, $30 Chalk Hill, $50 Bethel Heights, $65 Bergstrom) look like glass or half bottle prices rather than bottles at a Grand Award house; the format is written as unknown, not guessed.
Diamond Creek: the snippet gives $220 for 'Diamond Creek varieties' with no bottling (Gravelly Meadow, Red Rock Terrace, Volcanic Hill) and no vintage.
Harlan Estate is a vertical per Wine Spectator 2021, but no vintages or prices were found. Opus One vintages 2011, 2014, 2015, 2016 were found with no prices. Caymus: no vintages or prices.

Not found in any snippet: Screaming Eagle, Promontory, Spottswoode, Williams Selyem, Littorai, Aubert, Turley, any Walla Walla Syrah, any New Zealand wine, any Australian wine on the New Orleans list, any Chilean wine. Absence from a snippet is not absence from the list.

The Washington lines (Sixto Moxee 2013 $75, Waterbrook Reserve 2013 $52) and Catena Malbec $35 may come from a 2017 PDF on neworleans-food.com whose restaurant is not named in the snippet; held at low confidence.

Brennan's of Houston is a separate restaurant: its 2020 half price list (Houston Chronicle) and its 2022 wine list (getbento PDF) surfaced repeatedly and are recorded only as not this restaurant, never for the pack.

Glass list conflict: Argyle Brut Willamette Valley 2022 $15, Peter Michael L'Esprit des Pavots 2014 Coravin $60.00 and Drouhin Vaudon Chablis $23.00 appear on the house's own Cocktails & Wine By The Glass page, which the guide (p49) calls older than the Binwise glass list of 26 September. Whether any is still poured is unknown.

Cellar size: Wine Spectator listing figures of 3,635 selections and 19,415 bottles sit beside the house's 'over 14,000 bottles' and a cellar tour page's '15,000 bottles' and 'nearly 1400 selections'; the figures are of different dates and none is dated in the snippet.
No half bottle from the new world was found; the five 375 ml halves found are Champagne and Trento.
Chappellet Mountain Cuvée is printed as 2024, which is very young for a Napa red in October 2026; confirm the vintage on the list.
No pairing guidance from the house was found for any of these bottles; pairings for the Codex must be written as expert reasoning, marked as such.
